newsitem.title: CHAD: CHAD GRANTS AMNESTY TO FORMER REBELS IN OIL ZONE.
newsitem.headline: CHAD GRANTS AMNESTY TO FORMER REBELS IN OIL ZONE.

text.p: Chad's President Idriss Deby has signed a decree granting amnesty to supporters of a rebel movement which operated in an oil-rich corner of the south of the impoverished nation, state radio reported on Saturday.

The amnesty covered all members of the Armed Forces for the Federal Republic (FARF) and was part of a peace deal signed in the southern town of Moundou on April 18 by the government and the former rebel group, it said.
"The amnesty concerns all FARF militants and sympathisers jailed or prosecuted for membership of the rebel movement," the radio said.
Sources close to the movement said that FARF leader Laokien Barde had been reluctant to return to the capital NDjamena from the south because of security fears.
Chad has discovered significant reserves of oil in the predominantly Christian south and north of Lake Chad.
The government has reached preliminary agreement with foreign oil companies on exploiting the oil and also envisages a pipeline to a sea terminal in Cameroon. Chad is landlocked.

Deby, a former guerrilla leader from the Moslem north, seized power in a 1990 French-backed coup after decades of civil war or conflict with Libya. After repeated electoral delays, he won a multi-party presidential election in July.
His Patriotic Salvation Movement (MPS) won 63 of parliament's 125 seats in elections in January and February.
